Innosuisse Innolink - Innovationsprojekt (Entwurf)  -  Seite 1
Application Number: F1-000 Synthetic
Start Date: 01.03.2027
End Date: 28.02.2029
Duration: 24 months
Thematic Area: ICT
Cluster: Advanced Manufacturing / Industrial AI
Requested Innosuisse Funding incl. Overhead: CHF 258'000

1 Introduction
Application Name and Abstract
Application name
QUALIMON — KI-gestützte Qualitätsüberwachung für Produktionslinien
Application Name in English
QUALIMON — AI-based Quality Monitoring for Production Lines
Abstract (wird in Aramis publiziert)
QUALIMON develops an AI-based monitoring module for industrial production lines. The system aims to detect quality deviations earlier, reduce scrap and support better maintenance decisions. [[Angabe ergänzen: konkreter Nutzen und Validierung]]

Executive summary (wird nicht in Aramis publiziert)
Industrial production companies often detect quality deviations too late. As a result, defective batches, rework and unplanned downtime create avoidable costs. QUALIMON addresses this issue by combining machine signals, quality measurements and process context in an AI-supported monitoring module.
The project develops a prototype that detects abnormal production patterns and explains potential causes to process engineers. The implementation partner expects a 20 percent reduction in scrap and a 30 percent faster detection of critical deviations. These values are project targets and still require baseline data, measurement method and validation during the pilot.
The research partner contributes expertise in data modelling, explainable AI, validation design and industrial analytics. The solution will be tested on synthetic and pilot production data before integration into the implementation partner's monitoring environment.
[[Angabe ergänzen: baseline, measurement method, validation moment]]

Independence of Research and Implementation Partners
Explanations and Comments
The project partners declare that they are financially independent. No ownership relation above the relevant threshold is known at this stage. A final verification of ownership and financial dependencies is still required before submission.

Partners
Research Partner: Swiss Applied AI Lab — Fiktives Schweizer Forschungsinstitut mit Fokus auf Industrial AI
Implementation Partner: Alpine Monitoring Systems AG — Fiktives Schweizer KMU im Bereich Produktionsüberwachung
Pilot Site: Helvetic Components Factory — Fiktive Pilotanlage für Produktionsdaten

3 Value Creation
Open Editor
Business targets and business model
The implementation partner plans to commercialize QUALIMON as an add-on module for existing production monitoring systems. The target customers are Swiss industrial SMEs with automated production lines, recurring quality checks and a need for earlier deviation detection.
The solution is expected to reduce scrap by 20 percent and increase the speed of quality deviation detection by 30 percent. Based on internal assumptions, a medium-sized production site could save up to CHF 300'000 per year through reduced waste, fewer rework cycles and better process stability. These assumptions are not yet supported by external market evidence.
Customers and market access
The primary customer group consists of industrial companies in precision manufacturing, plastics processing and component assembly. The first pilot customer is expected to validate the prototype in an operational production setting.
The go-to-market plan is still incomplete. The project team plans to use pilot results, customer demonstrations and industry events to reach first customers after the project.
Competition and USP
Existing competitors offer general predictive-maintenance or machine-monitoring tools. QUALIMON aims to focus specifically on quality deviations and root-cause explanations for process engineers.
[[Angabe ergänzen: Marktgrösse, Wettbewerber, Zahlungsbereitschaft, Go-to-Market, belastbare Quelle]]

4 Solution
Open Editor
State of the art
Current industrial monitoring systems use rule-based thresholds, statistical process control and predictive-maintenance models. These approaches can detect anomalies, but they often provide limited explanation of why a quality deviation occurs and how it relates to process parameters.
Novelty of the solution
QUALIMON combines machine signals, quality measurements and process context in an explainable AI module. The system should identify early deviation patterns and propose possible causes.
The expected technical goals are:
- 20 percent reduction in scrap
- 30 percent faster detection of critical deviations
- at least 85 percent precision in detecting relevant deviation events
The baseline, measurement method and validation time point are not yet fully defined.
Preliminary work
The implementation partner has access to production monitoring data and quality reports from pilot lines. The research partner has experience with explainable AI and industrial analytics. The exact data quality, annotation process and legal basis for using the production data still need to be clarified.
Partner suitability
The implementation partner provides pilot access, domain knowledge and industrial validation. The research partner provides AI methodology and evaluation expertise. Evidence for partner track record and infrastructure should still be linked.
IPR / FTO
No patent search or Freedom-to-Operate analysis has been completed yet. The project team assumes that the main innovation will be protected as software know-how and trade secret, but the ownership of newly developed models, interfaces and datasets still needs to be clarified between the partners.
[[Angabe ergänzen: concrete SOTA comparison, data source details, training data quality, validation design, IPR/FTO strategy]]

5 Project Setup
Planned Hours
Explanation
The project includes coordination, reporting, partner alignment and preparation of review meetings. Management work is planned across the project duration. The exact distribution between project management, technical coordination and reporting still needs to be clarified.

Financial Overview

Own contribution implementation partner: CHF 150'000
Cash contribution implementation partner: CHF 12'000
Requested funding: CHF 258'000
Project duration: 24 months
